title: Performance Optimization: Parallelism & Caching ⚡
description: Use prefetch, cache, autotune, and interleaving to feed your GPU without starvation.

slides.title: The Perfect Pipeline 🏎️
slides.content:
# Goal: GPU Never Waits for Data

A well‑optimised pipeline performs:
- Reading
- Decoding
- Augmentation
- Batching

All on CPU, **in parallel** with GPU training. The magic ingredients:
- **Prefetch**
- **Parallel map**
- **Interleave**
- **Caching**
- **Autotune**

> Analogy: A kitchen where sous‑chefs (CPU) prepare ingredients while the head chef (GPU) cooks continuously.

slides.title: Prefetch & Autotune
slides.codeSnippet:
dataset = dataset.prefetch(buffer_size=tf.data.AUTOTUNE)
# buffer_size: how many batches to prepare in advance. AUTOTUNE chooses the best value dynamically.

quizData.question: What does `prefetch` do?

options.text: Loads the entire dataset into memory
Prepares the next batch while the current one is being processed

quizData.explanation: Prefetch creates a buffer that prepares the next batch(es) in background, overlapping CPU and GPU work.

slides.title: Caching: Store in Memory or Disk 💾
slides.content:
# Avoid Re‑reading Data Every Epoch

- `dataset.cache()` stores the dataset after the first epoch.
- If the dataset fits in RAM, caching eliminates disk I/O after epoch 1.
- Can also cache to a local file: `dataset.cache('/tmp/my_cache')`.

**Place cache after `map` and `batch` if you want to cache the processed version.**

slides.title: Optimised Pipeline Example
slides.codeSnippet:
dataset = tf.data.Dataset.list_files('data/train/*.jpg')
dataset = dataset.interleave(
    lambda x: tf.data.Dataset.from_tensor_slices([x]),
    cycle_length=tf.data.AUTOTUNE,
    num_parallel_calls=tf.data.AUTOTUNE
)
dataset = dataset.map(load_and_preprocess, num_parallel_calls=tf.data.AUTOTUNE)
dataset = dataset.batch(32)
dataset = dataset.cache()          # cache after batching
dataset = dataset.prefetch(tf.data.AUTOTUNE)

slides.title: Caching Large Datasets ⚠️
slides.content: If your processed dataset is larger than RAM, don't cache in memory. Use a file cache or skip caching altogether.

slides.title: Benchmark Your Pipeline ⏱️
slides.content: Add `tf.data.experimental.OptimizationOptions` or use `model.fit` with `verbose=1` and watch GPU utilisation via `nvidia‑smi`. If GPU utilisation is low, your pipeline is the bottleneck.
